title: A busy MP4 lands at the size the Export sheet said
goal: When a screen recording is full of fast-moving detail, like scrolling a page of text, the MP4 that lands can be twice the size the Export sheet quoted, so someone who picked Small to get under a chat limit finds their file does not fit.
notes: Measured 2026-09-25 on an idle machine (the-export-size-test-fails-about-one-run-in-thre), 3 s 1280x800 scrolling-text source (VideoExportBudgetTests.scrollingText is the same picture), bytes landed against recipe.expectedBytes: at 300 px/s High 1,564,796 vs 1,382,400, Standard 1,104,754 vs 921,600, Small 546,480 vs 324,000 (+69%); at 900 px/s High 1,733,042, Standard 1,548,584 (+68%), Small 830,895 vs 324,000 (+156%). RecordingExport.weight shows min(budget, measuredCost) with 'about', so the sheet shows at most the budget. The system H.264 encoder treats AVVideoAverageBitRateKey as a target and overshoots on detail-heavy frames (key frame every 2 s). Tried adding kVTCompressionPropertyKey_DataRateLimits [bitrate/8 bytes, 1 s] via AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey: Small at 900 px/s came to 490,901 (still +52%) and High at 300 px/s fell to 979,188 (-29%, under), so a hard limit alone is not the answer; a second-pass or a quality-based (not bitrate-based) estimate may be. The software encoder (EnableHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder false) overshoots far worse: Small 1,256,251. Pure noise overshoots ~10x at every choice but is not screen material. Under concurrent encodes the sizes also swing wildly (Standard 1.1 to 3.1 MB), which nothing in the app can control. || 2026-09-27 run: shipped. MovieCompression (PhotonzMedia) holds the encoder (kVTCompressionPropertyKey_DataRateLimits [1.3x budget/8 bytes, 1s]) only when VideoExportSample.holdsToBudget says the unheld stretches overshoot (holdAbove 1.0). Always-on cap was rejected: it took the 1080p Retina talk from 2,120,001 to 1,214,169 bytes/min at High (any cap <=2x; 10x made it 2.52 MB). Sheet weigh: ExportWeigh.measure + EditorState.weighVideo -> DocumentMovieWriter.weigh; RecordingExportDialog -> AppCoordinator.weighRecording -> VideoExporter.weighMP4. Stretches: VideoExportSample.writingOrder (<=12s whole, else 6x2s GOP-aligned behind a warm-up copy of the first; counted from 2s via MovieCompression.pictureBytes). RecordingExport.weight uses weighing bytes for MP4 (.about). Final isolated numbers (landed/budget; weigh==landed to the byte): 300px/s 0.92/0.92/0.95, 900px/s 0.97/1.30/1.70. Under the full suite's parallel encodes an unheld borderline picture swung 1.20 -> 1.57, hence holdAbove 1.0 and lightest-of-three in tests.
acceptance: On a 3 second 1280x800 recording of text scrolling at 300 and at 900 pixels a second, each of High, Standard and Small lands within 25 per cent of the size the sheet shows for it
The same holds on the easy recordings the export tests already use, so an easy recording is not pushed far under its number
If the encoder cannot be held to the number, the sheet shows a number that the file really lands near, and a test says which

log.note: reproduced 2026-09-28 (XP probe test, quiet machine): 300px/s High 1.13 Std 1.20 Small 1.70; 900px/s 1.25/1.68/2.56 of budget. Tried: CBR, key interval 10, no reordering, max QP 51, lower asks (ABR floors: Small900 never under 739K at 0.2x ask), software encoder (ignores bitrate: 19x). DataRateLimits [1.3x budget over 1s] single pass: 300: 0.92/0.92/0.96, 900: 0.95/1.28/1.64, easy unchanged. Small900 floor is the hardware encoder's (CBR 0.1x ask still 420K = 1.30), so no rate control meets 25% there: the sheet must measure. Adversarial: a person picking Small for a chat limit reads the number before pressing Export, so the number must be right before the write; formulas off the source file cannot see busyness (fixture sources at High land 1.27M vs 1.32M yet Small lands 0.96 vs 1.64), so only an encode can tell. Premiere shows an estimate that is bitrate x length and is also wrong on busy material; beating it means measuring. Plan: DRL in both writers + sampled weigh (2s GOP-aligned stretches, up to 6) on the Next Export sheet that corrects the about number.

built and verified: BusyVideoSizeTests + core tests green, full suite 10246 tests green, walks a-busy-recording-says-what-it-weighs (sheet 1.8 MB / 1.8 MB landed at Small, 2.1/2.1 Standard), an-edited-recording (1.00-1.04x, now held to 1.25), export-a-video-at-1080p (17 MB, sheet 19 MB, 1.06x), an-editing-session (1.21x), export-keeps-to-the-in-and-out (1.00-1.01x), export-card-while-writing ok. Adversarial after: the number moving up a moment after the sheet opens could read as unsteady (in audit evaluate); Small of a very busy recording still exceeds Small's budget (encoder floor) and the sheet says so (audit rough). Left rough, not filed: document export spends a few seconds weighing first (progress card counts it as the first 5%); sheet runs ~20% high on the editing-session doc (errs safe). No follow-up filed: nothing broken, rough items are in the audit for the user to react to.

Busy MP4s now land within 25% of the Export sheet's number at every choice. Writers hold the encoder to its budget only when stretches show the picture would overshoot (easy recordings unchanged, verified on the 1080p talk); where the encoder's floor wins (Standard/Small of fast scrolling), both Export sheets weigh stretches in the background and show the real size. Commit 799ef6a2. Verified: BusyVideoSizeTests + core tests, full suite 10246 green, walks a-busy-recording-says-what-it-weighs (sheet 1.8 MB, 1.8 MB landed at Small), an-edited-recording (held to 1.25x), export-a-video-at-1080p, an-editing-session, export-keeps-to-the-in-and-out, export-card-while-writing all ok.
